content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: 1:1 Beátus vir, qui non ábiit in consílio impiórum, et in via peccatórum non stetit, * et in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit:
content.english: 1:1 Blessed is the man who hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stood in the way of sinners, * nor sat in the chair of pestilence.

segments.t: Beátus vir, qui non ábiit in consílio impiórum, et in via peccatórum non stetit, * et in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit:

content.latin: 1:2 Sed in lege Dómini volúntas eius, * et in lege eius meditábitur die ac nocte.
content.english: 1:2 But his will is in the law of the Lord, * and on his law he shall meditate day and night.

segments.t: Sed in lege Dómini volúntas eius, * et in lege eius meditábitur die ac nocte.

content.latin: 1:3 Et erit tamquam lignum, quod plantátum est secus decúrsus aquárum, * quod fructum suum dabit in témpore suo:
content.english: 1:3 And he shall be like a tree which is planted near the running waters, * which shall bring forth its fruit, in due season.

segments.t: Et erit tamquam lignum, quod plantátum est secus decúrsus aquárum, * quod fructum suum dabit in témpore suo:

content.latin: 1:3 Et fólium eius non défluet: * et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, prosperabúntur.
content.english: 1:3 And his leaf shall not fall off: * and all whatsoever he shall do shall prosper.

segments.t: Et fólium eius non défluet: * et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, prosperabúntur.

content.latin: 1:4 Non sic ímpii, non sic: * sed tamquam pulvis, quem próicit ventus a fácie terræ.
content.english: 1:4 Not so the wicked, not so: * but like the dust, which the wind driveth from the face of the earth.

segments.t: Non sic ímpii, non sic: * sed tamquam pulvis, quem próicit ventus a fácie terræ.

content.latin: 1:5 Ídeo non resúrgent ímpii in iudício: * neque peccatóres in concílio iustórum.
content.english: 1:5 Therefore the wicked shall not rise again in judgment: * nor sinners in the council of the just.

segments.t: Ídeo non resúrgent ímpii in iudício: * neque peccatóres in concílio iustórum.

content.latin: 1:6 Quóniam novit Dóminus viam iustórum: * et iter impiórum períbit.

segments.t: Quóniam novit Dóminus viam iustórum: * et iter impiórum períbit.

segments.t: Psalmus 2

content.latin: 2:1 Quare fremuérunt gentes: * et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?
content.english: 2:1 Why have the Gentiles raged, * and the people devised vain things?

segments.t: Quare fremuérunt gentes: * et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?

content.latin: 2:2 Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum * advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum eius.
content.english: 2:2 The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes met together, * against the Lord and against his Christ.

segments.t: Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum * advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum eius.

content.latin: 2:3 Dirumpámus víncula eórum: * et proiciámus a nobis iugum ipsórum.
content.english: 2:3 Let us break their bonds asunder: * and let us cast away their yoke from us.

segments.t: Dirumpámus víncula eórum: * et proiciámus a nobis iugum ipsórum.

content.latin: 2:4 Qui hábitat in cælis, irridébit eos: * et Dóminus subsannábit eos.
content.english: 2:4 He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them: * and the Lord shall deride them.

segments.t: Qui hábitat in cælis, irridébit eos: * et Dóminus subsannábit eos.

content.latin: 2:5 Tunc loquétur ad eos in ira sua, * et in furóre suo conturbábit eos.
content.english: 2:5 Then shall he speak to them in his anger, * and trouble them in his rage.

segments.t: Tunc loquétur ad eos in ira sua, * et in furóre suo conturbábit eos.

content.latin: 2:6 Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum eius, * prǽdicans præcéptum eius.
content.english: 2:6 But I am appointed king by him over Sion his holy mountain, * preaching his commandment.

segments.t: Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum eius, * prǽdicans præcéptum eius.

content.latin: 2:7 Dóminus dixit ad me: * Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
content.english: 2:7 The Lord hath said to me: * Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee.

segments.t: Dóminus dixit ad me: * Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.

content.latin: 2:8 Póstula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam, * et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.
content.english: 2:8 Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, * and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession.

segments.t: Póstula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam, * et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.

content.latin: 2:9 Reges eos in virga férrea, * et tamquam vas fíguli confrínges eos.
content.english: 2:9 Thou shalt rule them with a rod of iron, * and shalt break them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.

segments.t: Reges eos in virga férrea, * et tamquam vas fíguli confrínges eos.

content.latin: 2:10 Et nunc, reges, intellégite: * erudímini, qui iudicátis terram.
content.english: 2:10 And now, O ye kings, understand: * receive instruction, you that judge the earth.

segments.t: Et nunc, reges, intellégite: * erudímini, qui iudicátis terram.

content.latin: 2:11 Servíte Dómino in timóre: * et exsultáte ei cum tremóre.
content.english: 2:11 Serve ye the Lord with fear: * and rejoice unto him with trembling.

segments.t: Servíte Dómino in timóre: * et exsultáte ei cum tremóre.

content.latin: 2:12 Apprehéndite disciplínam, nequándo irascátur Dóminus, * et pereátis de via iusta.
content.english: 2:12 Embrace discipline, lest at any time the Lord be angry, * and you perish from the just way.

segments.t: Apprehéndite disciplínam, nequándo irascátur Dóminus, * et pereátis de via iusta.

content.latin: 2:13 Cum exárserit in brevi ira eius: * beáti omnes qui confídunt in eo.
content.english: 2:13 When his wrath shall be kindled in a short time, * blessed are all they that trust in him.

segments.t: Cum exárserit in brevi ira eius: * beáti omnes qui confídunt in eo.

segments.t: Psalmus 3

content.latin: 3:2 Dómine, quid multiplicáti sunt qui tríbulant me? * multi insúrgunt advérsum me.
content.english: 3:2 Why, O Lord, are they multiplied that afflict me? * many are they who rise up against me.

segments.t: Dómine, quid multiplicáti sunt qui tríbulant me? * multi insúrgunt advérsum me.

content.latin: 3:3 Multi dicunt ánimæ meæ: * Non est salus ipsi in Deo eius.
content.english: 3:3 Many say to my soul: * There is no salvation for him in his God.

segments.t: Multi dicunt ánimæ meæ: * Non est salus ipsi in Deo eius.

content.latin: 3:4 Tu autem, Dómine, suscéptor meus es, * glória mea, et exáltans caput meum.
content.english: 3:4 But thou, O Lord art my protector, * my glory, and the lifter up of my head.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, suscéptor meus es, * glória mea, et exáltans caput meum.

content.latin: 3:5 Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.
content.english: 3:5 I have cried to the Lord with my voice: * and he hath heard me from his holy hill.

segments.t: Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.

content.latin: 3:6 Ego dormívi, et soporátus sum: * et exsurréxi, quia Dóminus suscépit me.
content.english: 3:6 I have slept and taken my rest: * and I have risen up, because the Lord hath protected me.

segments.t: Ego dormívi, et soporátus sum: * et exsurréxi, quia Dóminus suscépit me.

content.latin: 3:7 Non timébo míllia pópuli circumdántis me: * exsúrge, Dómine, salvum me fac, Deus meus.
content.english: 3:7 I will not fear thousands of the people, surrounding me: * arise, O Lord; save me, O my God.

segments.t: Non timébo míllia pópuli circumdántis me: * exsúrge, Dómine, salvum me fac, Deus meus.

content.latin: 3:8 Quóniam tu percussísti omnes adversántes mihi sine causa: * dentes peccatórum contrivísti.
content.english: 3:8 For thou hast struck all them who are my adversaries without cause: * thou hast broken the teeth of sinners.

segments.t: Quóniam tu percussísti omnes adversántes mihi sine causa: * dentes peccatórum contrivísti.

content.latin: 3:9 Dómini est salus: * et super pópulum tuum benedíctio tua.

segments.t: Dómini est salus: * et super pópulum tuum benedíctio tua.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.latin: De Actibus Apostolórum
content.english: Lesson from the Acts of Apostles
Acts 6:1-6

content.latin: 1 In diébus illis, crescénte número discipulórum, factum est murmur Græcórum advérsus Hebrǽos, eo quod despiceréntur in ministério cotidiáno víduæ eórum.
content.english: 1 And in those days, the number of the disciples increasing, there arose a murmuring of the Greeks against the Hebrews, for that their widows were neglected in the daily ministration.

segments.t: In diébus illis, crescénte número discipulórum, factum est murmur Græcórum advérsus Hebrǽos, eo quod despiceréntur in ministério cotidiáno víduæ eórum.

content.latin: 2 Convocántes autem duódecim multitúdinem discipulórum, dixérunt: Non est æquum nos derelínquere verbum Dei et ministráre mensis.
content.english: 2 Then the twelve calling together the multitude of the disciples, said: It is not reason that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables.

segments.t: Convocántes autem duódecim multitúdinem discipulórum, dixérunt: Non est æquum nos derelínquere verbum Dei et ministráre mensis.

content.latin: 3 Consideráte ergo, fratres, viros ex vobis boni testimónii, septem, plenos Spíritu Sancto et sapiéntia, quos constituámus super hoc opus.
content.english: 3 Wherefore, brethren, look ye out among you seven men of good reputation, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business.

segments.t: Consideráte ergo, fratres, viros ex vobis boni testimónii, septem, plenos Spíritu Sancto et sapiéntia, quos constituámus super hoc opus.

content.latin: 4 Nos vero oratióni et ministério verbi instántes érimus.
content.english: 4 But we will give ourselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry of the word.

segments.t: Nos vero oratióni et ministério verbi instántes érimus.

content.latin: 5 Et plácuit sermo coram omni multitúdine. Et elegérunt Stéphanum virum plenum fide et Spíritu Sancto, et Philíppum, et Próchorum, et Nicánorem, et Timónem, et Pármenam, et Nicoláum, ádvenam Antiochénum.
content.english: 5 And the saying was liked by all the multitude. And they chose Stephen, a man full of faith, and of the Holy Ghost, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolas, a proselyte of Antioch.

segments.t: Et plácuit sermo coram omni multitúdine. Et elegérunt Stéphanum virum plenum fide et Spíritu Sancto, et Philíppum, et Próchorum, et Nicánorem, et Timónem, et Pármenam, et Nicoláum, ádvenam Antiochénum.

content.latin: 6 Hos statuérunt ante conspéctum Apostolórum: et orántes imposuérunt eis manus.
content.english: 6 These they set before the apostles; and they praying, imposed hands upon them.

segments.t: Hos statuérunt ante conspéctum Apostolórum: et orántes imposuérunt eis manus.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Stéphanus autem plenus grátia et fortitúdine,
content.english: ℟. And Stephen, full of grace and power

segments.t: Stéphanus autem plenus grátia et fortitúdine,

content.latin: * Faciébat prodígia et signa magna in pópulo.
content.english: * Did great wonders and miracles among the people.

content.latin: ℣. Surrexérunt quidam de synagóga disputántes cum Stéphano: et non póterant resístere sapiéntiæ, et Spirítui qui loquebátur.
content.english: ℣. There arose certain of the synagogue, disputing with Stephen; and they were not able to resist the wisdom, and the Spirit which spoke.

segments.t: Surrexérunt quidam de synagóga disputántes cum Stéphano: et non póterant resístere sapiéntiæ, et Spirítui qui loquebátur.

content.latin: ℟. Faciébat prodígia et signa magna in pópulo.
content.english: ℟. Did great wonders and miracles among the people.

segments.t: Faciébat prodígia et signa magna in pópulo.

content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.
content.english: Benediction. May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: 7 Et verbum Dómini crescébat, et multiplicabátur númerus discipulórum in Ierúsalem valde: multa étiam turba sacerdótum obediébat fídei.
content.english: 7 And the word of the Lord increased; and the number of the disciples was multiplied in Jerusalem exceedingly: a great multitude also of the priests obeyed the faith.

segments.t: Et verbum Dómini crescébat, et multiplicabátur númerus discipulórum in Ierúsalem valde: multa étiam turba sacerdótum obediébat fídei.

content.latin: 8 Stéphanus autem plenus grátia et fortitúdine, faciébat prodígia et signa magna in pópulo.
content.english: 8 And Stephen, full of grace and fortitude, did great wonders and signs among the people.

segments.t: Stéphanus autem plenus grátia et fortitúdine, faciébat prodígia et signa magna in pópulo.

content.latin: 9 Surrexérunt autem quidam de synagóga, quæ appellátur Libertinórum, et Cyrenénsium et Alexandrinórum, et eórum qui erant a Cilícia, et Asia, disputántes cum Stéphano:
content.english: 9 Now there arose some of that which is called the synagogue of the Libertines, and of the Cyrenians, and of the Alexandrians, and of them that were of Cilicia and Asia, disputing with Stephen.

segments.t: Surrexérunt autem quidam de synagóga, quæ appellátur Libertinórum, et Cyrenénsium et Alexandrinórum, et eórum qui erant a Cilícia, et Asia, disputántes cum Stéphano:

content.latin: 10 Et non póterant resístere sapiéntiæ, et Spirítui qui loquebátur.
content.english: 10 And they were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit that spoke.

segments.t: Et non póterant resístere sapiéntiæ, et Spirítui qui loquebátur.

content.latin: 54 Audiéntes autem hæc, dissecabántur córdibus suis, et stridébant déntibus in eum.
content.english: 54 Now hearing these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed with their teeth at him.

segments.t: Audiéntes autem hæc, dissecabántur córdibus suis, et stridébant déntibus in eum.

content.english: ℟. All that sat in the council, looking steadfastly on Stephen, saw

content.english: * His face as it had been the face of an angel standing among them.

content.latin: ℣. Plenus grátia et fortitúdine, faciébat prodígia et signa magna in pópulo.
content.english: ℣. Full of grace and power, he did great wonders and miracles among the people.

segments.t: Plenus grátia et fortitúdine, faciébat prodígia et signa magna in pópulo.

content.english: Benediction. May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.

Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.

content.latin: 55 Cum autem esset plenus Spíritu Sancto, inténdens in cælum, vidit glóriam Dei, et Iesum stantem a dextris Dei. Et ait: Ecce vídeo cælos apértos, et Fílium hóminis stantem a dextris Dei.
content.english: 55 But he, being full of the Holy Ghost, looking up steadfastly to heaven, saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God. And he said: Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God.

segments.t: Cum autem esset plenus Spíritu Sancto, inténdens in cælum, vidit glóriam Dei, et Iesum stantem a dextris Dei. Et ait: Ecce vídeo cælos apértos, et Fílium hóminis stantem a dextris Dei.

content.latin: 56 Exclamántes autem voce magna, continuérunt aures suas, et ímpetum fecérunt unanímiter in eum.
content.english: 56 And they crying out with a loud voice, stopped their ears, and with one accord ran violently upon him.

segments.t: Exclamántes autem voce magna, continuérunt aures suas, et ímpetum fecérunt unanímiter in eum.

content.latin: 57 Et eiciéntes eum extra civitátem lapidábant: et testes deposuérunt vestiménta sua secus pedes adolescéntis, qui vocabátur Saulus.
content.english: 57 And casting him forth without the city, they stoned him; and the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man, whose name was Saul.

segments.t: Et eiciéntes eum extra civitátem lapidábant: et testes deposuérunt vestiménta sua secus pedes adolescéntis, qui vocabátur Saulus.

content.latin: 58 Et lapidábant Stéphanum, invocántem et dicéntem: Dómine Iesu, súscipe spíritum meum.
content.english: 58 And they stoned Stephen, invoking, and saying: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.

segments.t: Et lapidábant Stéphanum, invocántem et dicéntem: Dómine Iesu, súscipe spíritum meum.

content.latin: 59 Pósitis autem génibus, clamávit voce magna, dicens: Dómine, ne státuas illis hoc peccátum. Et cum hoc dixísset, obdormívit in Dómino.
content.english: 59 And falling on his knees, he cried with a loud voice, saying: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep in the Lord.

segments.t: Pósitis autem génibus, clamávit voce magna, dicens: Dómine, ne státuas illis hoc peccátum. Et cum hoc dixísset, obdormívit in Dómino.

content.latin: Ant. Fílii hóminum * scitóte quia Dóminus sanctum suum mirificávit.
content.english: Ant. O ye sons of men, * know that the Lord hath set apart him that is holy for Himself.

segments.t: Ant.
Fílii hóminum * scitóte quia Dóminus sanctum suum mirificávit.

content.latin: Psalmus 4 [4]
content.english: Psalm 4 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 4

content.latin: 4:2 Cum invocárem exaudívit me Deus iustítiæ meæ: * in tribulatióne dilatásti mihi.
content.english: 4:2 When I called upon him, the God of my justice heard me: * when I was in distress, thou hast enlarged me.

segments.t: Cum invocárem exaudívit me Deus iustítiæ meæ: * in tribulatióne dilatásti mihi.

content.latin: 4:2 Miserére mei, * et exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: 4:2 Have mercy on me: * and hear my prayer.

segments.t: Miserére mei, * et exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: 4:3 Fílii hóminum, úsquequo gravi corde? * ut quid dilígitis vanitátem, et quǽritis mendácium?
content.english: 4:3 O ye sons of men, how long will you be dull of heart? * Why do you love vanity, and seek after lying?

segments.t: Fílii hóminum, úsquequo gravi corde? * ut quid dilígitis vanitátem, et quǽritis mendácium?

content.latin: 4:4 Et scitóte quóniam mirificávit Dóminus sanctum suum: * Dóminus exáudiet me cum clamávero ad eum.
content.english: 4:4 Know ye also that the Lord hath made his holy one wonderful: * the Lord will hear me when I shall cry unto him.

segments.t: Et scitóte quóniam mirificávit Dóminus sanctum suum: * Dóminus exáudiet me cum clamávero ad eum.

content.latin: 4:5 Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: * quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, in cubílibus vestris compungímini.
content.english: 4:5 Be ye angry, and sin not: * the things you say in your hearts, be sorry for them upon your beds.

segments.t: Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: * quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, in cubílibus vestris compungímini.

content.latin: 4:6 Sacrificáte sacrifícium iustítiæ, et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?
content.english: 4:6 Offer up the sacrifice of justice, and trust in the Lord: * many say, Who sheweth us good things?

segments.t: Sacrificáte sacrifícium iustítiæ, et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?

content.latin: 4:7 Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.
content.english: 4:7 The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us: * thou hast given gladness in my heart.

segments.t: Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.

content.latin: 4:8 A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.
content.english: 4:8 By the fruit of their corn, their wine, and oil, * they are multiplied.

segments.t: A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.

content.latin: 4:9 In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;
content.english: 4:9 In peace in the selfsame * I will sleep, and I will rest:

segments.t: In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;

content.latin: 4:10 Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe * constituísti me.
content.english: 4:10 For thou, O Lord, singularly * hast settled me in hope.

segments.t: Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe * constituísti me.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Fílii hóminum scitóte quia Dóminus sanctum suum mirificávit.
content.english: Ant. O ye sons of men, know that the Lord hath set apart him that is holy for Himself.

segments.t: Ant.
Fílii hóminum scitóte quia Dóminus sanctum suum mirificávit.

content.latin: Ant. Scuto bonæ voluntátis * tuæ coronásti eum Dómine.
content.english: Ant. O Lord, Thou hast compassed him * with thy favour as with a shield.

segments.t: Ant.
Scuto bonæ voluntátis * tuæ coronásti eum Dómine.

content.latin: Psalmus 5 [5]
content.english: Psalm 5 [5]

segments.t: Psalmus 5

content.latin: 5:2 Verba mea áuribus pércipe, Dómine, * intéllege clamórem meum.
content.english: 5:2 Give ear, O Lord, to my words * understand my cry.

segments.t: Verba mea áuribus pércipe, Dómine, * intéllege clamórem meum.

content.latin: 5:3 Inténde voci oratiónis meæ, * Rex meus et Deus meus.
content.english: 5:3 Hearken to the voice of my prayer, * O my King and my God.

segments.t: Inténde voci oratiónis meæ, * Rex meus et Deus meus.

content.latin: 5:4 Quóniam ad te orábo: * Dómine, mane exáudies vocem meam.
content.english: 5:4 For to thee will I pray: * O Lord, in the morning thou shalt hear my voice.

segments.t: Quóniam ad te orábo: * Dómine, mane exáudies vocem meam.

content.latin: 5:5 Mane astábo tibi et vidébo: * quóniam non Deus volens iniquitátem tu es.
content.english: 5:5 In the morning I will stand before thee, and will see: * because thou art not a God that willest iniquity.

segments.t: Mane astábo tibi et vidébo: * quóniam non Deus volens iniquitátem tu es.

content.latin: 5:6 Neque habitábit iuxta te malígnus: * neque permanébunt iniústi ante óculos tuos.
content.english: 5:6 Neither shall the wicked dwell near thee: * nor shall the unjust abide before thy eyes.

segments.t: Neque habitábit iuxta te malígnus: * neque permanébunt iniústi ante óculos tuos.

content.latin: 5:7 Odísti omnes, qui operántur iniquitátem: * perdes omnes, qui loquúntur mendácium.
content.english: 5:7 Thou hatest all the workers of iniquity: * thou wilt destroy all that speak a lie.

segments.t: Odísti omnes, qui operántur iniquitátem: * perdes omnes, qui loquúntur mendácium.

content.latin: 5:7 Virum sánguinum et dolósum abominábitur Dóminus: * ego autem in multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ.
content.english: 5:7 The bloody and the deceitful man the Lord will abhor. * But as for me in the multitude of thy mercy,

segments.t: Virum sánguinum et dolósum abominábitur Dóminus: * ego autem in multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ.

content.latin: 5:8 Introíbo in domum tuam: * adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum in timóre tuo.
content.english: 5:8 I will come into thy house; * I will worship towards thy holy temple, in thy fear.

segments.t: Introíbo in domum tuam: * adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum in timóre tuo.

content.latin: 5:9 Dómine, deduc me in iustítia tua: * propter inimícos meos dírige in conspéctu tuo viam meam.
content.english: 5:9 Conduct me, O Lord, in thy justice: * because of my enemies, direct my way in thy sight.

segments.t: Dómine, deduc me in iustítia tua: * propter inimícos meos dírige in conspéctu tuo viam meam.

content.latin: 5:10 Quóniam non est in ore eórum véritas: * cor eórum vanum est.
content.english: 5:10 For there is no truth in their mouth: * their heart is vain.

segments.t: Quóniam non est in ore eórum véritas: * cor eórum vanum est.

content.latin: 5:11 Sepúlcrum patens est guttur eórum, linguis suis dolóse agébant, * iúdica illos, Deus.
content.english: 5:11 Their throat is an open sepulchre: they dealt deceitfully with their tongues: * judge them, O God.

segments.t: Sepúlcrum patens est guttur eórum, linguis suis dolóse agébant, * iúdica illos, Deus.

content.latin: 5:11 Décidant a cogitatiónibus suis, secúndum multitúdinem impietátum eórum expélle eos, * quóniam irritavérunt te, Dómine.
content.english: 5:11 Let them fall from their devices: according to the multitude of their wickednesses cast them out: * for they have provoked thee, O Lord.

segments.t: Décidant a cogitatiónibus suis, secúndum multitúdinem impietátum eórum expélle eos, * quóniam irritavérunt te, Dómine.

content.latin: 5:12 Et læténtur omnes, qui sperant in te, * in ætérnum exsultábunt: et habitábis in eis.
content.english: 5:12 But let all them be glad that hope in thee: * they shall rejoice for ever, and thou shalt dwell in them.

segments.t: Et læténtur omnes, qui sperant in te, * in ætérnum exsultábunt: et habitábis in eis.

content.latin: 5:12 Et gloriabúntur in te omnes, qui díligunt nomen tuum, * quóniam tu benedíces iusto.

content.latin: Heri celebrávimus temporálem sempitérni Regis nostri natálem: hódie celebrámus triumphálem mílitis passiónem. Heri enim Rex noster trábea carnis indútus, de aula úteri virginális egrédiens, visitáre dignátus est mundum: hódie miles de tabernáculo córporis éxiens, triumphátor migrávit ad cælum. Ille, sempitérnæ Deitátis maiestáte serváta, servíle cinctórium carnis assúmens, in huius sǽculi campum pugnatúrus intrávit; iste, depósitis corruptibílibus córporis induméntis, ad cæli palátium perénniter regnatúrus ascéndit. Ille descéndit carne velátus, iste ascéndit sánguine laureátus.
content.english: Yesterday we were celebrating the birth in time of our Eternal King; today we celebrate the victory, through suffering, of one of His soldiers. Yesterday our King was pleased to come forth from His royal palace of the Virgin's womb, clothed in a robe of flesh, to visit the world; today His soldier, laying aside the tabernacle of the body, entereth in triumph into the heavenly palaces. The One, preserving unchanged that glory of the Godhead which He had before the world was, girded Himself with the form of a servant, and entered the arena of this world to fight sin; the other taketh off the garments of this corruptible body, and entereth into the heavenly mansions, where he will reign for ever. The One cometh down, veiled in flesh; the other goeth up, clothed in a robe of glory, red with blood.

content.latin: Ascéndit iste lapidántibus Iudǽis, quia ille descéndit lætántibus Angelis. Glória in excélsis Deo, heri sancti Angeli exsultántes cantavérunt: hódie Stéphanum lætántes in suum consórtium suscepérunt. Heri Dóminus exívit de útero Vírginis: hódie miles egréssus est de ergástulo carnis. Heri Christus pro nobis pannis est involútus: hódie Stéphanus stola est ab eo immortalitátis indútus. Heri præsépis angústia Christum portávit infántem: hódie imménsitas cæli suscépit Stéphanum triumphántem. Solus Dóminus descéndit, ut multos eleváret: humiliávit se Rex noster, ut suos mílites exaltáret.
content.english: The One cometh down amid the jubilation of angels; the other goeth up amid the stoning of the Jews. Yesterday the holy angels were singing, Glory to God in the highest; today there is joy among them, for they receive Stephen into their company. Yesterday the Lord came forth from the Virgin's womb; today His soldier is delivered from the prison of the body. Yesterday Christ was for our sakes wrapped in swaddling bands; today He girdeth Stephen with a robe of immortality. Yesterday the new-born Christ lay in a narrow manger; today Stephen entereth victorious into the boundless heavens. The Lord came down alone that He might raise many up; our King humbled Himself that He might set His soldiers in high places.

content.latin: Necessárium tamen nobis est, fratres, agnóscere, quibus armis præcínctus Stéphanus sævítiam Iudæórum pótuit superáre, ut ita meruísset felíciter triumpháre. Stéphanus ergo, ut nóminis sui corónam meruísset accípere, caritátem pro armis habébat, et per ipsam ubíque vincébat. Per caritátem Dei sæviéntibus Iudǽis non cessit: per caritátem próximi pro lapidántibus intercéssit. Per caritátem arguébat errántes, ut corrigeréntur: per caritátem pro lapidántibus orábat, ne puniréntur. Caritátis virtúte subníxus, vicit Saulum crudéliter sæviéntem; et quem hábuit in terra persecutórem, in cælo méruit habére consórtem.
content.english: Why brethren, it behoveth us to consider with what arms Stephen was able, amid all the cruelty of the Jews, to remain more than conqueror, and worthily to attain to so blessed a triumph. Stephen, in that struggle which brought him to the crown whereof his name is a prophecy, had for armour the love of God and man, and by it he remained victorious on all hands. The love of God strengthened him against the cruelty of the Jews; and the love of his neighbour made him pray even for his murderers. Through love he rebuked the wandering, that they might be corrected; through love he prayed for them that stoned him, that they might not be punished. By the might of his love he overcame Saul his cruel persecutor; and earned for a comrade in heaven, the very man who had done him to death upon earth.

content.latin: Hoc quod ántea dixerámus, Impléte mensúram patrum vestrórum; ad persónam Dómini pertinére, eo quod occidéndus esset ab eis, potest et ad discípulos eius reférri, de quibus nunc dicit: Ecce ego mitto ad vos prophétas, et sapiéntes, et scribas. Simúlque obsérva, iuxta Apóstolum scribéntem ad Corínthios, vária esse dona discipulórum Christi; álios prophétas, qui ventúra prædícent; álios sapiéntes, qui novérunt quando débeant proférre sermónem; álios scribas in lege doctíssimos, ex quibus lapidátus est Stéphanus, Paulus occísus, crucifíxus Petrus, flagelláti in Actibus Apostolórum discípuli.
content.english: We have already remarked that the Lord's words, Fill ye up the measure of your fathers, 32, refer in the first place to Himself, Whom the Jews afterwards put to death. In a secondary sense it may likewise be applied to His disciples, of whom He saith, Behold, I send unto you Prophets, and wise men, and Scribes. Here observe that, according to the Apostle writing to the Corinthians, 1 Cor. xii. 4, there are diversities of gifts among Christ's followers. Some are Prophets of that which is to come; some are wise men, who know the due season for rebuke and exhortation; some are Scribes learned in the law. And of these they stoned Stephen, slew Paul with the sword, crucified Peter, and scourged the Disciples mentioned in the Acts of the Apostles. v, 40; xvi, 23.

content.latin: Quǽrimus, quis iste sit Zacharías fílius Barachíæ: quia multos légimus Zacharías. Et ne líbera nobis tribuerétur erróris facúltas, ádditum est: Quem occidístis inter templum et altáre. In divérsis divérsa legi: et débeo singulórum opiniónes pónere. Alii Zacharíam fílium Barachíæ dicunt, qui in duódecim prophétis undécimus est, patrísque in eo nomen conséntit: sed ubi occísus sit inter templum et altáre, Scriptúra non lóquitur; máxime cum tempóribus eius vix ruínæ templi fúerint. Alii Zacharíam patrem Ioánnis intellégi volunt, ex quibúsdam apocryphórum sómniis approbántes, quod proptérea occísus sit, quia Salvatóris prædicáverit advéntum.
content.english: It is a subject of dispute among commentators who is meant by Zacharias the son of Barachias. We read of several persons of the name of Zacharias. But here, in order to prevent any mistake, it is particularly said, Whom ye slew between the temple and the altar. I have read various opinions in various places upon this question, and I will give each. First, some hold that Zacharias the son of Barachias is the eleventh of the twelve Minor Prophets; and this opinion is supported by the father's name. But the Bible nowhere telleth us that this Prophet was slain between the temple and the altar; and it is hardly possible that he can have been, for in his time it could scarcely be said that even the ruins of the temple were in existence. Secondly, others maintain that this Zacharias was Zacharias, the father of John the Baptist. This interpretation is derived from the dreams of the Apocryphal Gospels, wherein it is asserted that he was martyred for preaching Christ's coming.

content.latin: Alii istum volunt esse Zacharíam, qui occísus est a Ioas rege Iudæ inter templum et altáre, sicut Regum narrat história. Sed observándum, quod ille Zacharías non sit fílius Barachíæ, sed fílius Ióiadæ sacerdótis: unde et Scriptúra refert: Non fuit recordátus Ioas patris eius Ióiadæ, quia sibi fecísset bona. Cum ergo et Zacharíam teneámus et occisiónis conséntiat locus: quǽrimus, quare Barachíæ dicátur fílius, et non Ióiadæ? Barachía lingua nostra Benedíctus Dómini dícitur, et sacerdótis Ióiadæ iustítia Hebrǽo nómine demonstrátur. In Evangélio, quo utúntur Nazaréni, pro fílio Barachíæ, fílium Ióiadæ reperímus scriptum.
content.english: A third school will have it that this Zacharias, the son of Barachias, was that Zacharias of whom we read, in Chron. xxiv. 22, that he was slain by Joash, king of Judah, between the temple and the altar. Against this it is to be remarked, that that Zacharias was not the son of Barachias, but of Jehoiada the priest; whence it is written, Joash remembered not the kindness which Jehoiada his father had done to him. The question therefore ariseth, if this opinion be true, why, the name and manner of death both agreeing with this explanation, Zacharias is called the son, not of Jehoiada, but of Barachias. In Hebrew, Barachias signifieth the Blessed of the Lord, and Jehoiada proves his Righteousness. In the Gospel used by the Nazarenes the name of Jehoiada is used instead of Barachias.

content.english: Kneel for the following verse We therefore pray thee, help thy servants, * whom thou hast redeemed with thy precious Blood.

segments.t: Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus
Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.

content.latin: Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
content.english: Make them to be numbered with thy Saints, * in glory everlasting.

content.latin: Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
content.english: O Lord, save thy people, * and bless thine heritage.

content.latin: Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
content.english: Govern them, * and lift them up for ever.

content.latin: Per síngulos dies * benedícimus te.
content.english: Day by day * we magnify thee;

content.latin: Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: During the following verse, by local custom, all make a profound bow. And we worship thy Name * ever, world without end.

segments.t: Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem
Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
content.english: Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us * this day without sin.

content.latin: Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
content.english: O Lord, have mercy upon us, * have mercy upon us.

content.latin: Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
content.english: O Lord, let thy mercy lighten upon us, * as our trust is in thee.

content.latin: In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.
content.english: O Lord, in thee have I trusted, * let me never be confounded.

content.latin: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi separandæ sint.
content.english: Skip the rest, unless praying separately.

segments.t: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi separandæ sint.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Da nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, imitári quod cólimus: ut discámus et inimícos dilígere; quia eius natalícia celebrámus, qui novit étiam pro persecutóribus exoráre Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum:
content.english: Grant us, we beseech thee, O Lord, so to imitate what we revere, that we may learn to love even our enemies; for we celebrate the heavenly birthday of him who knew how to pray for his very persecutors to our Lord Jesus Christ:

content.latin: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Who with thee liveth and reigneth, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: ℣. Benedicámus Dómino.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedicámus Dómino.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℣. Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
content.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

segments.t: Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

segments.t: Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

segments.t: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.

content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.english: Alleluia.

content.english: Psalm 92 [1]

content.latin: 92:1 Dóminus regnávit, decórem indútus est: * indútus est Dóminus fortitúdinem, et præcínxit se.
content.english: 92:1 The Lord hath reigned, he is clothed with beauty: * the Lord is clothed with strength, and hath girded himself.

segments.t: Dóminus regnávit, decórem indútus est: * indútus est Dóminus fortitúdinem, et præcínxit se.

content.latin: 92:1 Étenim firmávit orbem terræ, * qui non commovébitur.
content.english: 92:1 For he hath established the world * which shall not be moved.

segments.t: Étenim firmávit orbem terræ, * qui non commovébitur.

content.latin: 92:2 Paráta sedes tua ex tunc: * a sǽculo tu es.
content.english: 92:2 Thy throne is prepared from of old: * thou art from everlasting.

segments.t: Paráta sedes tua ex tunc: * a sǽculo tu es.

content.latin: 92:3 Elevavérunt flúmina, Dómine: * elevavérunt flúmina vocem suam.
content.english: 92:3 The floods have lifted up, O Lord: * the floods have lifted up their voice.

segments.t: Elevavérunt flúmina, Dómine: * elevavérunt flúmina vocem suam.

content.latin: 92:3 Elevavérunt flúmina fluctus suos, * a vócibus aquárum multárum.
content.english: 92:3 The floods have lifted up their waves, * with the noise of many waters.

segments.t: Elevavérunt flúmina fluctus suos, * a vócibus aquárum multárum.

content.latin: 92:4 Mirábiles elatiónes maris: * mirábilis in altis Dóminus.
content.english: 92:4 Wonderful are the surges of the sea: * wonderful is the Lord on high.

segments.t: Mirábiles elatiónes maris: * mirábilis in altis Dóminus.

content.latin: 92:5 Testimónia tua credibília facta sunt nimis: * domum tuam decet sanctitúdo, Dómine, in longitúdinem diérum.
content.english: 92:5 Thy testimonies are become exceedingly credible: * holiness becometh thy house, O Lord, unto length of days.

segments.t: Testimónia tua credibília facta sunt nimis: * domum tuam decet sanctitúdo, Dómine, in longitúdinem diérum.

content.latin: Ant. Lápides torréntis * illi dulces fuérunt: ipsum sequúntur omnes ánimæ iustæ.
content.english: Ant. The stones of the brook * were sweet to him; all the souls of the righteous follow him.

Lápides torréntis * illi dulces fuérunt: ipsum sequúntur omnes ánimæ iustæ.

content.english: Psalm 99 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 99

content.latin: 99:2 Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra: * servíte Dómino in lætítia.
content.english: 99:2 Sing joyfully to God, all the earth: * serve ye the Lord with gladness.

segments.t: Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra: * servíte Dómino in lætítia.

content.latin: 99:2 Introíte in conspéctu eius, * in exsultatióne.
content.english: 99:2 Come in before his presence * with exceeding great joy.

segments.t: Introíte in conspéctu eius, * in exsultatióne.

content.latin: 99:3 Scitóte quóniam Dóminus ipse est Deus: * ipse fecit nos, et non ipsi nos.
content.english: 99:3 Know ye that the Lord he is God: * he made us, and not we ourselves.

segments.t: Scitóte quóniam Dóminus ipse est Deus: * ipse fecit nos, et non ipsi nos.

content.latin: 99:3 Pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius: * introíte portas eius in confessióne, átria eius in hymnis: confitémini illi.
content.english: 99:3 We are his people and the sheep of his pasture. * Go ye into his gates with praise, into his courts with hymns: and give glory to him.

segments.t: Pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius: * introíte portas eius in confessióne, átria eius in hymnis: confitémini illi.

content.latin: 99:4 Laudáte nomen eius: quóniam suávis est Dóminus, in ætérnum misericórdia eius, * et usque in generatiónem et generatiónem véritas eius.
content.english: 99:4 Praise ye his name: for the Lord is sweet, his mercy endureth for ever, * and his truth to generation and generation.

segments.t: Laudáte nomen eius: quóniam suávis est Dóminus, in ætérnum misericórdia eius, * et usque in generatiónem et generatiónem véritas eius.

content.english: Ant. O my God, my soul followeth hard after thee, * for my flesh hath been stoned for thy sake.

Adhǽsit ánima mea * post te, quia caro mea lapidáta est pro te, Deus meus.

content.latin: Psalmus 62 [3]
content.english: Psalm 62 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 62

content.latin: 62:2 Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.
content.english: 62:2 O God, my God, * to thee do I watch at break of day.

segments.t: Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.

content.latin: 62:2 Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.
content.english: 62:2 For thee my soul hath thirsted; * for thee my flesh, O how many ways!

segments.t: Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.

content.latin: 62:3 In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.
content.english: 62:3 In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: * so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, to see thy power and thy glory.

segments.t: In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.

content.latin: 62:4 Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.
content.english: 62:4 For thy mercy is better than lives: * thee my lips shall praise.

segments.t: Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.

content.latin: 62:5 Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.
content.english: 62:5 Thus will I bless thee all my life long: * and in thy name I will lift up my hands.

segments.t: Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.

content.latin: 62:6 Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.
content.english: 62:6 Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: * and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips.

segments.t: Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.

content.latin: 62:7 Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.
content.english: 62:7 If I have remembered thee upon my bed, I will meditate on thee in the morning: * because thou hast been my helper.

segments.t: Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.

content.latin: 62:8 Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.
content.english: 62:8 And I will rejoice under the covert of thy wings: my soul hath stuck close to thee: * thy right hand hath received me.

segments.t: Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.

content.latin: 62:10 Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.
content.english: 62:10 But they have sought my soul in vain, they shall go into the lower parts of the earth: * they shall be delivered into the hands of the sword, they shall be the portions of foxes.

segments.t: Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.

content.latin: 62:12 Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.
content.english: 62:12 But the king shall rejoice in God, all they shall be praised that swear by him: * because the mouth is stopped of them that speak wicked things.

segments.t: Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.

content.latin: 3:57 Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:57 All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:58 Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:58 O ye angels of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye heavens, bless the Lord:

segments.t: Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:59 Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:59 O all ye waters that are above the heavens, bless the Lord: * O all ye powers of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:60 Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:60 O ye sun and moon, bless the Lord: * O ye stars of heaven, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:61 Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.
content.english: 3:61 O every shower and dew, bless ye the Lord: * O all ye spirits of God, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:62 Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:62 O ye fire and heat, bless the Lord: * O ye cold and heat, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:63 Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:63 O ye dews and hoar frosts, bless the Lord: * O ye frost and cold, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:64 Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.
content.english: 3:64 O ye ice and snow, bless the Lord: * O ye nights and days, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:65 Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.
content.english: 3:65 O ye light and darkness, bless the Lord: * O ye lightnings and clouds, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:66 Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:66 O let the earth bless the Lord: * let it praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:67 Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.
content.english: 3:67 O ye mountains and hills, bless the Lord: * O all ye things that spring up in the earth, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:68 Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.
content.english: 3:68 O ye fountains, bless the Lord: * O ye seas and rivers, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:69 Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:69 O ye whales, and all that move in the waters, bless the Lord: * O all ye fowls of the air, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:70 Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.
content.english: 3:70 O all ye beasts and cattle, bless the Lord: * O ye sons of men, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:71 Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:71 O let Israel bless the Lord: * let them praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:72 Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:72 O ye priests of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye servants of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:73 Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.
content.english: 3:73 O ye spirits and souls of the just, bless the Lord: * O ye holy and humble of heart, bless the Lord.

content.latin: Apud Ephesum natális sancti Ioánnis, Apóstoli et Evangelístæ, qui, post Evangélii scriptiónem, post exsílii relegatiónem et Apocalýpsim divínam, usque ad Traiáni Príncipis témpora persevérans, totíus Asiæ fundávit rexítque Ecclésias, ac tandem, conféctus sénio, sexagésimo octávo post passiónem Dómini anno mórtuus est, et iuxta eándem urbem sepúltus.
content.english: At Ephesus, the holy Apostle and Evangelist John. After the writing of his Gospel after his return from exile, and after the Revelation which God gave unto him, he lived on until the time of the Emperor Trajan, and founded and governed the churches of all Asia. He died of old age in the sixty-eighth year after the death of Christ (about the year 101), and was buried hard by the city of Ephesus.

content.latin: Constantinópoli sanctórum Confessórum Theodóri et Theóphanis fratrum, qui, a puerítia in Palæstinénsi sancti Sabbæ monastério nutríti, cum póstea pro sanctárum Imáginum cultu advérsus Leónem Arménum strénue decertárent, eius iussu verbéribus affécti sunt et exsílio relegáti. Sed, eódem Leóne mórtuo, rursus Theóphilo Imperatóri, qui eádem impietáte detinebátur, constánter resisténtes, verbéribus íterum cæsi et in exsílium pulsi sunt, ubi Theodórus in cárcere exspirávit. Theóphanes vero, pace demum Ecclésiæ réddita, factus est Nicǽnæ civitátis Epíscopus, et confessiónis glória præclárus quiévit in Dómino.
content.english: At Alexandria, holy Maximus, Pope of that See, who was eminently worthy to be called a confessor (in the year 282).

content.latin: Alexandríæ sancti Máximi Epíscopi, qui satis clarus et insígnis título confessiónis efféctus est.
content.english: At Constantinople the holy brethren Theodore (Grapt) and Theophanes. They were bred up from their childhood in the monastery of St. Saba, and afterwards stoutly contended for the honouring of holy images against the Emperor Leo the Armenian, for the which he caused them to be beaten and sent into exile, and after his death they still stoutly withstood the Emperor Theophilus, who was held captive by the same ungodliness, for the which he also caused them to be again beaten and driven into exile. Theodore died in prison, but Theophanes, after that peace was given back to the Church, was made Bishop of Nice, and fell asleep in peace in the Lord (ninth century).

content.latin: ℣. Réspice in servos tuos, Dómine, et in ópera tua, et dírige fílios eórum.
content.english: ℣. Look upon thy servants and upon thy works: and direct their children.

segments.t: Réspice in servos tuos, Dómine, et in ópera tua, et dírige fílios eórum.

content.latin: ℟. Et sit splendor Dómini Dei nostri super nos, et ópera mánuum nostrárum dírige super nos, et opus mánuum nostrárum dírige.
content.english: ℟. And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us. Direct thou the works of our hands; yea, the work of our hands do thou direct.

segments.t: Et sit splendor Dómini Dei nostri super nos, et ópera mánuum nostrárum dírige super nos, et opus mánuum nostrárum dírige.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Dirígere et sanctificáre, régere et gubernáre dignáre, Dómine Deus, Rex cæli et terræ, hódie corda et córpora nostra, sensus, sermónes et actus nostros in lege tua, et in opéribus mandatórum tuórum: ut hic et in ætérnum, te auxiliánte, salvi et líberi esse mereámur, Salvátor mundi: Qui vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: O Lord, Almighty God, King of heaven and earth, Saviour of the world, bless, lead, rule and govern our hearts and bodies, our senses, words and deeds today, following thy law and commandments, that here and for eternity with thy help we shall be saved in freedom. Who livest and reignest, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Dies et actus nostros in sua pace dispónat Dóminus omnípotens.
content.english: Benediction. May Almighty God arrange our deeds and our day in His peace.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Dies et actus nostros in sua pace dispónat Dóminus omnípotens.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: Ipsi períbunt, tu autem permanébis; et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent: et velut amíctum mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.
content.english: They shall perish, but thou shalt continue: and they shall all grow old as a garment. And as a vesture shalt thou change them, and they shall be changed: but thou art the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.english: ℣. Our help is ✠ in the name of the Lord,

segments.t: Adiutórium nostrum ✠ in nómine Dómini.

content.latin: ℟. Qui fecit cælum et terram.
content.english: ℟. Who made heaven and earth.

segments.t: Qui fecit cælum et terram.

content.latin: ℣. Benedícite.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless.

segments.t: Benedícite.

content.latin: ℟. Deus.
content.english: ℟. God.

segments.t: Deus.

content.latin: Benedictio. Dóminus nos benedícat, ✠ et ab omni malo deféndat, et ad vitam perdúcat ætérnam. Et fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
content.english: Benediction. May the Lord bless us, ✠ protect us from all evil and bring us to everlasting life. And may the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Dóminus nos benedícat, ✠ et ab omni malo deféndat, et ad vitam perdúcat ætérnam. Et fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.

content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

Clamor meus, * Dómine, ad te pervéniat: non avértas fáciem tuam a me.
Psalmus 101(2-13)

content.latin: 101:2 Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam: * et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: 101:2 Hear, O Lord, my prayer: * and let my cry come to thee.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam: * et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: 101:3 Non avértas fáciem tuam a me: * in quacúmque die tríbulor, inclína ad me aurem tuam.
content.english: 101:3 Turn not away thy face from me: * in the day when I am in trouble, incline thy ear to me.

segments.t: Non avértas fáciem tuam a me: * in quacúmque die tríbulor, inclína ad me aurem tuam.

content.latin: 101:3 In quacúmque die invocávero te, * velóciter exáudi me.
content.english: 101:3 In what day soever I shall call upon thee, * hear me speedily.

segments.t: In quacúmque die invocávero te, * velóciter exáudi me.

content.latin: 101:4 Quia defecérunt sicut fumus dies mei: * et ossa mea sicut crémium aruérunt.
content.english: 101:4 For my days are vanished like smoke: * and my bones are grown dry like fuel for the fire.

segments.t: Quia defecérunt sicut fumus dies mei: * et ossa mea sicut crémium aruérunt.

content.latin: 101:5 Percússus sum ut fænum, et áruit cor meum: * quia oblítus sum comédere panem meum.
content.english: 101:5 I am smitten as grass, and my heart is withered: * because I forgot to eat my bread.

segments.t: Percússus sum ut fænum, et áruit cor meum: * quia oblítus sum comédere panem meum.

content.latin: 101:6 A voce gémitus mei * adhǽsit os meum carni meæ.
content.english: 101:6 Through the voice of my groaning, * my bone hath cleaved to my flesh.

segments.t: A voce gémitus mei * adhǽsit os meum carni meæ.

content.latin: 101:7 Símilis factus sum pellicáno solitúdinis: * factus sum sicut nyctícorax in domicílio.
content.english: 101:7 I am become like to a pelican of the wilderness: * I am like a night raven in the house.

segments.t: Símilis factus sum pellicáno solitúdinis: * factus sum sicut nyctícorax in domicílio.

content.latin: 101:8 Vigilávi, * et factus sum sicut passer solitárius in tecto.
content.english: 101:8 I have watched, * and am become as a sparrow all alone on the housetop.

segments.t: Vigilávi, * et factus sum sicut passer solitárius in tecto.

content.latin: 101:9 Tota die exprobrábant mihi inimíci mei: * et qui laudábant me, advérsum me iurábant.
content.english: 101:9 All the day long my enemies reproached me: * and they that praised me did swear against me.

segments.t: Tota die exprobrábant mihi inimíci mei: * et qui laudábant me, advérsum me iurábant.

content.latin: 101:10 Quia cínerem tamquam panem manducábam, * et potum meum cum fletu miscébam.
content.english: 101:10 For I did eat ashes like bread, * and mingled my drink with weeping.

segments.t: Quia cínerem tamquam panem manducábam, * et potum meum cum fletu miscébam.

content.latin: 101:11 A fácie iræ et indignatiónis tuæ: * quia élevans allisísti me.
content.english: 101:11 Because of thy anger and indignation: * for having lifted me up thou hast thrown me down.

segments.t: A fácie iræ et indignatiónis tuæ: * quia élevans allisísti me.

content.latin: 101:12 Dies mei sicut umbra declinavérunt: * et ego sicut fænum árui.
content.english: 101:12 My days have declined like a shadow, * and I am withered like grass.

segments.t: Dies mei sicut umbra declinavérunt: * et ego sicut fænum árui.

content.latin: 101:13 Tu autem, Dómine, in ætérnum pérmanes: * et memoriále tuum in generatiónem et generatiónem.
content.english: 101:13 But thou, O Lord, endurest for ever: * and thy memorial to all generations.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, in ætérnum pérmanes: * et memoriále tuum in generatiónem et generatiónem.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
Psalmus 101(14-23)

content.latin: 101:14 Tu exsúrgens miseréberis Sion: * quia tempus miseréndi eius, quia venit tempus.
content.english: 101:14 Thou shalt arise and have mercy on Sion: * for it is time to have mercy on it, for the time is come.

segments.t: Tu exsúrgens miseréberis Sion: * quia tempus miseréndi eius, quia venit tempus.

content.latin: 101:15 Quóniam placuérunt servis tuis lápides eius: * et terræ eius miserebúntur.
content.english: 101:15 For the stones thereof have pleased thy servants: * and they shall have pity on the earth thereof.

segments.t: Quóniam placuérunt servis tuis lápides eius: * et terræ eius miserebúntur.

content.latin: 101:16 Et timébunt gentes nomen tuum, Dómine, * et omnes reges terræ glóriam tuam.
content.english: 101:16 And the Gentiles shall fear thy name, O Lord, * and all the kings of the earth thy glory.

segments.t: Et timébunt gentes nomen tuum, Dómine, * et omnes reges terræ glóriam tuam.

content.latin: 101:17 Quia ædificávit Dóminus Sion: * et vidébitur in glória sua.
content.english: 101:17 For the Lord hath built up Sion: * and he shall be seen in his glory.

segments.t: Quia ædificávit Dóminus Sion: * et vidébitur in glória sua.

content.latin: 101:18 Respéxit in oratiónem humílium: * et non sprevit precem eórum.
content.english: 101:18 He hath had regard to the prayer of the humble: * and he hath not despised their petition.

segments.t: Respéxit in oratiónem humílium: * et non sprevit precem eórum.

content.latin: 101:19 Scribántur hæc in generatióne áltera: * et pópulus, qui creábitur, laudábit Dóminum:
content.english: 101:19 Let these things be written unto another generation: * and the people that shall be created shall praise the Lord:

segments.t: Scribántur hæc in generatióne áltera: * et pópulus, qui creábitur, laudábit Dóminum:

content.latin: 101:20 Quia prospéxit de excélso sancto suo: * Dóminus de cælo in terram aspéxit:
content.english: 101:20 Because he hath looked forth from his high sanctuary: * from heaven the Lord hath looked upon the earth.

segments.t: Quia prospéxit de excélso sancto suo: * Dóminus de cælo in terram aspéxit:

content.latin: 101:21 Ut audíret gémitus compeditórum: * ut sólveret fílios interemptórum:
content.english: 101:21 That he might hear the groans of them that are in fetters: * that he might release the children of the slain:

segments.t: Ut audíret gémitus compeditórum: * ut sólveret fílios interemptórum:

content.latin: 101:22 Ut annúntient in Sion nomen Dómini: * et laudem eius in Ierúsalem.
content.english: 101:22 That they may declare the name of the Lord in Sion: * and his praise in Jerusalem;

segments.t: Ut annúntient in Sion nomen Dómini: * et laudem eius in Ierúsalem.

content.latin: 101:23 In conveniéndo pópulos in unum, * et reges ut sérviant Dómino.
content.english: 101:23 When the people assemble together, * and kings, to serve the Lord.

segments.t: In conveniéndo pópulos in unum, * et reges ut sérviant Dómino.

Psalmus 101(24-29)

content.latin: 101:24 Respóndit ei in via virtútis suæ: * Paucitátem diérum meórum núntia mihi.
content.english: 101:24 He answered him in the way of his strength: * Declare unto me the fewness of my days.

segments.t: Respóndit ei in via virtútis suæ: * Paucitátem diérum meórum núntia mihi.

content.latin: 101:25 Ne révoces me in dimídio diérum meórum: * in generatiónem et generatiónem anni tui.
content.english: 101:25 Call me not away in the midst of my days: * thy years are unto generation and generation.

segments.t: Ne révoces me in dimídio diérum meórum: * in generatiónem et generatiónem anni tui.

content.latin: 101:26 Inítio tu, Dómine, terram fundásti: * et ópera mánuum tuárum sunt cæli.
content.english: 101:26 In the beginning, O Lord, thou foundedst the earth: * and the heavens are the works of thy hands.

segments.t: Inítio tu, Dómine, terram fundásti: * et ópera mánuum tuárum sunt cæli.

content.latin: 101:27 Ipsi períbunt, tu autem pérmanes: * et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent.
content.english: 101:27 They shall perish but thou remainest: * and all of them shall grow old like a garment:

segments.t: Ipsi períbunt, tu autem pérmanes: * et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent.

content.latin: 101:28 Et sicut opertórium mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: * tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.
content.english: 101:28 And as a vesture thou shalt change them, and they shall be changed. * But thou art always the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail.

segments.t: Et sicut opertórium mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: * tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.

content.latin: 101:29 Fílii servórum tuórum habitábunt: * et semen eórum in sǽculum dirigétur.
content.english: 101:29 The children of thy servants shall continue: * and their seed shall be directed for ever.

segments.t: Fílii servórum tuórum habitábunt: * et semen eórum in sǽculum dirigétur.

content.latin: Da nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, imitári quod cólimus: ut discámus et inimícos dilígere; quia eius natalícia celebrámus, qui novit étiam pro persecutóribus exoráre Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum:
content.english: Grant us, we beseech thee, O Lord, so to imitate what we revere, that we may learn to love even our enemies; for we celebrate the heavenly birthday of him who knew how to pray for his very persecutors to our Lord Jesus Christ:

content.latin: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Who with thee liveth and reigneth, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.

content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Rector potens, verax Deus,
content.english: O God of truth, O Lord of might,

content.latin: Qui témperas rerum vices,
content.english: Who orderest time and change aright,

content.latin: Splendóre mane illúminas,
content.english: Who send’st the early morning ray,

content.latin: Et ígnibus merídiem:
content.english: And light’st the glow of perfect day:

content.latin: Exstíngue flammas lítium,
content.english: Extinguish thou each sinful fire,

content.latin: Aufer calórem nóxium,
content.english: And banish every ill desire;

content.latin: Confer salútem córporum,
content.english: And while thou keep’st the body whole,

content.latin: Verámque pacem córdium.
content.english: Shed forth thy peace upon the soul.

content.latin: Præsta, Pater piíssime,
content.english: Almighty Father, hear our cry,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, our Lord most High,

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito
content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,

content.latin: Regnans per omne sǽculum.
content.english: Doth live and reign eternally.

content.english: Amen.
